name: Eich Well
notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-05 (session 2) via NDWR WellLogQuery, owner search 'EICH': single exact match 'EICH, PAUL', Basin 087, T18N R20E Sec 21 SW, log 10437, completed 1969-01-25, depth 100 ft. Preferred over several superficially similar surnames in the same result set (Heidenreich, Eichelberger, Eichmann, Reichman, Reichlin, Meich) because this is the only literal 'Eich' owner in the area, and it sits ~403m from the separately-resolved DeMonte well and ~885m from Herz Domestic -- consistent with Klein et al. (2007) Figure 1's tight NDOT/Curti/Herz/DiMonte/Eich monitor-well cluster just N of the geothermal field. Minor caveat, not fully resolved: this log's total depth (100 ft) doesn't exactly match the NDEP permit table's description 'Eich (Shallow, 45 ft.)' -- plausibly a difference between total drilled depth and a specific sampling/perforation depth used for monitoring, rather than a wrong-well match.

The two Basin-087 candidates found were a 7-log cluster at T19N R19E Sec36 (39.4716,-119.7899, ~7-8km N of the cluster) and a single 'NDOT RIGHT OF WAY' log at T17N R20E Sec23 (39.317972,-119.707695, ~6-7km S/E) -- both rejected as too far away. Klein's map places NDOT immediately beside Curti/Herz/Soccer Field, so the true well is either logged under a different owner name (e.g. the actual maintenance-station name, or 'State of Nevada'/'Department of Transportation' rather than the abbreviation 'NDOT'), or simply isn't captured by an owner-name search at all. Left unlocated -- a spatial (GIS/map-based) NDWR search of the cluster area, rather than further owner-name guesses, is the more promising next step.
